title.value: A Framework for Obtaining Accurate Posteriors of Strong Gravitational Lensing Parameters with Flexible Priors and Implicit Likelihoods using Density Estimation
title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote: A Framework for Obtaining Accurate Posteriors of Strong Gravitational Lensing Parameters with Flexible Priors and Implicit Likelihoods using Density Estimation

extractions.description: The paper presents an application of implicit likelihood inference using neural networks to predict macro-parameters of strong lensing systems. It introduces a Bayesian statistical framework for deep learning analysis of lensing systems, enabling explicit imposition of priors, accurate posterior estimations, and convergence to optimal posterior. The method involves training neural networks for regression to produce point estimates of lensing parameters, modeling their likelihood function using mixture density networks, and comparing results with approximate Bayesian neural networks. The study demonstrates accurate posterior production on a test set of strong lensing simulations, with efficient scaling for large upcoming sky surveys.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on a novel method using deep learning to analyze strong gravitational lensing systems, which primarily contributes to advancements in astrophysics and cosmology. While the techniques developed could potentially be applied to other fields, its direct and primary focus is not on climate change, ecological sustainability, or related Sustainable Development Goals. Therefore, sustainable development is not a central theme of this paper.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We report the application of implicit likelihood inference to the prediction of the macro-parameters of strong lensing systems with neural networks. This allows us to perform deep learning analysis of lensing systems within a well-defined Bayesian statistical framework to explicitly impose desired priors on lensing variables, to obtain accurate posteriors, and to guarantee convergence to the optimal posterior in the limit of perfect performance.
